why: `pop()` reads from the bottom of the stack with `shift()`, so Back closes the layer UNDER the one on screen: with Records open over Settings the player's Back dismisses Settings while Records stays, and a confirmation's Back removes the route it was raised over while the confirmation stays up. A plain LIFO pop is the entire mechanism behind the issue's "Back removes one overlay before one route", so this is the mutation that breaks that guarantee directly. Fails 2 of 15 in navigation.test.ts: `back pops the topmost layer, LIFO: [route a, route b] pops b then a` and `an overlay above a route is removed before the route, and each pop carries its own recorded origin and restore`, each at its first `pop()` assertion.
